questions.question:
D1 — Should the two new callers reuse lib/retry-after.ts or carry local parsers?
Project/branch/task: main — plan review of PLAN.md (import-worker and sync-route Retry-After parsing under the fixed scheduler contract).
ELI10: Both new files need to turn a Retry-After header (a number of seconds, an HTTP date, or nothing) into a wait time that is capped at one hour and falls back to a caller-chosen number when the header is junk. The scheduler already does exactly this through one shared function in lib/retry-after.ts, which has its own contract test. The plan drafts a fresh copy of that logic inside each new file. Two more copies means three places that must stay identical forever, while one import means the behavior cannot drift.
Stakes if we pick wrong: a copy that diverges, or an unpinned edge case, makes a worker or route wait a different time than the scheduler for the same header, and nobody notices until a backoff misbehaves in production.
Recommendation: A because the required behavior is identical by definition, the helper is already proven and tested, and it saves about 26 implementation lines; the extra contract assertions cost minutes and are the only proof that the "fixed" edge cases actually hold.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=7/10, C=4/10
Pros / cons:
A) Reuse helper, extend tests (recommended) (human: ~1.5 h / CC: ~5 min)
  ✅ Both callers import retrySeconds(value, now, fallback) from lib/retry-after.ts, the same call shape src/scheduler.ts:2 already uses, so semantics match by construction
  ✅ Adds the missing shared-contract assertions the callers depend on (empty or whitespace string returns fallback, "0" returns 0, past date returns 0, far-future date returns 3600, unsafe integer returns fallback, unparseable date returns the caller fallback) plus one integration test per caller that passes an explicit now and a non-default fallback
  ❌ Grows test/retry-after.test.ts by about 6-8 lines and widens the blast radius: a future helper bug or hardening change reaches scheduler, import-worker and sync-route at once
B) Reuse helper, existing tests (human: ~1 h / CC: ~3 min)
  ✅ Same import wiring and the same ~26-line implementation saving as A, with no change to the shared test file
  ✅ Lowest-touch diff: only the two new source files and their two integration tests
  ❌ The five existing assertions never exercise past dates, the date ceiling, empty strings or unsafe integers, so the "fixed" edge-case compatibility stays unproven at the shared layer
C) Local parser per caller (human: ~2 h / CC: ~5 min)
  ✅ Each caller is self-contained; a later change to lib/retry-after.ts cannot alter these two files
  ✅ Matches the plan as currently drafted, so no plan amendment is needed
  ❌ Adds about 28 duplicated lines, creates two more copies that must replicate every quirk of the runtime's Date.parse leniency to stay scheduler-compatible, and only integration tests guard each copy
Net: one import plus a handful of contract assertions buys guaranteed parity and a smaller diff; the only thing given up is isolation from future helper changes, which the plan says must be shared anyway.
